title: A Once in a 100 Year Investment Opportunity Just Started (Felix Nikolas Prehn on Where He's Buying)
creator: MarketBeat
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: MarketBeat guest Felix Nikolas Prehn lays out three value areas after the AI selloff: gold and miners, profitable power, and the big profitable hyperscalers, and warns against anything non-profitable. On gold, his thesis is that gold does not go up, the dollar goes down: with the Fed printing at astounding rates, gold at about $4,000 is a 10-plus-year safety play, a first-tracked BUY for MarketBeat. Among miners, Newmont (NEM) is a first-tracked BUY, a blue-chip miner generating real cash at $4,000/oz gold; Agnico Eagle (AEM) is a BUY reiterated; Wheaton Precious Metals (WPM) is a first-tracked BUY for its royalty and streaming model with no operational risk; Pan-American Silver (PAAS) is UNCERTAIN, watchlist only, down about 40% with a terrible short-term chart. He calls junior gold miners 'dangerous as hell' and says to avoid them. In power, Emerson Electric (EMR), Constellation Energy (CEG) and Vistra (VST) are all first-tracked BUYs: profitable generators down 30-40% with real power contracts, while the US needs far more electricity whatever happens to AI. Alphabet (GOOGL) is a BUY reiterated as the most obvious AI winner, down about 28-29%, and Uber (UBER) is a first-tracked BUY, now free-cash-flow positive with dominant mobility distribution. Micron (MU) softens to UNCERTAIN from CONDITIONAL_BUY: it could lose 50% and he does not like the odds. He also says to avoid small modular reactors and cash-flow-negative moonshots, and notes he sold Dollar General into Thursday's pop as a counterbalance trade.
